- When sentiment is consistently low or negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- If sentiment spikes sharply (e.g., >0.67) followed by rapid decline, model often overshoots and then undercorrects — cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high if sentiment rises then falls.
- If news volume is high and sentiment is neutral or positive, model tends to overestimate — apply 3–5% downward adjustment if news volume >3 and sentiment <0.67.
- Model often overestimates in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile — apply 2–5% downward bias for short-term forecasts if sentiment change >0.33.
- If sentiment is flat or trending downward, model tends to lag — add 1–3% upward bias to forecast if sentiment change is negative but recent price is rising.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–8% if sentiment is weak or news is low.
- Overshoot after sentiment spike: if model peaks >15% above recent high and sentiment drops within 3 days, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
